display.name: StackGres PostgreSQL
display.description: Health and capacity of a StackGres SGCluster from its postgres_exporter, Patroni and PgBouncer metrics, plus Kubernetes pod resources: HA and replication, connections and pooling, load and contention, I/O and cache, WAL and archiving, vacuum and growth. I/O and Vacuum sections start collapsed.

display.name: Archiver · failures
display.description: pg_stat_archiver_failed_count (increase). Any value above zero is worth a look at the archive logs.

filter.expression: cluster IN $cluster AND deployment_environment IN $deployment_environment AND resource.namespace IN $namespace AND pod IN $pod

display.name: Archiver · age of last archive (s)
display.description: Broken WAL archiving breaks PITR and backups and fills the disk. Minimum across pods: a replica does not archive, so its value freezes at the last failover and keeps growing. The minimum is the age of the most recent archive in the cluster, whichever pod is primary.

filter.expression: cluster IN $cluster AND deployment_environment IN $deployment_environment AND resource.namespace IN $namespace AND pod IN $pod

spec.legend: last archive age in the cluster (s)
spec.name: A

display.description: Disk reads vs buffer cache hits.

display.name: Replica lag in bytes (LSN)
display.description: patroni_xlog_location − patroni_xlog_replayed_location, clamped at 0: the two metrics are scraped at slightly different instants, so a lag near zero can come out slightly negative. Zero means below the measurement noise floor. Healthy under 10 MB; thresholds at 128 MB / 1 GB.

filter.expression: cluster IN $cluster AND deployment_environment IN $deployment_environment AND resource.namespace IN $namespace
cluster IN $cluster AND deployment_environment IN $deployment_environment AND resource.namespace IN $namespace

display.name: Replica lag in seconds
display.description: How long the replica is behind the primary (RPO). pg_replication_lag_seconds per pod: the primary reports 0, so the rising line is the replica, and it follows a failover without edits. It drops to 0 once received WAL is replayed, so 0 means 'caught up', not 'no traffic'. Max within each bucket to keep short spikes. Threshold at 60 s.

filter.expression: cluster IN $cluster AND deployment_environment IN $deployment_environment AND resource.namespace IN $namespace AND pod IN $pod

display.name: Locks by mode
display.description: pg_locks_count by mode. Sustained growth of ExclusiveLock / RowExclusiveLock means contention.

filter.expression: cluster IN $cluster AND deployment_environment IN $deployment_environment AND resource.namespace IN $namespace AND pod IN $pod

display.name: Longest transaction (s)
display.description: pg_stat_activity_max_tx_duration. Over 900 s it holds back vacuum, locks and xmin; look for idle in transaction.

filter.expression: cluster IN $cluster AND deployment_environment IN $deployment_environment AND resource.namespace IN $namespace AND pod IN $pod

display.name: Memory per pod (usage)
display.description: k8s.pod.memory.usage. PostgreSQL fills the page cache, so the working set sits near the limit by design; watch the trend, not the absolute value.

filter.expression: k8s.cluster.name IN $cluster AND k8s.pod.name IN $pod

display.name: Network I/O per pod (bytes/s)
display.description: k8s.pod.network.io (rate). Abnormal peaks often follow client retry storms.

filter.expression: k8s.cluster.name IN $cluster AND k8s.pod.name IN $pod

display.name: PgBouncer · active and waiting clients
display.description: cl_active (linked to a server) vs cl_waiting (queued). A sustained queue means a small pool or slow queries holding connections.

display.name: Database PVCs · % used
display.description: (1 − available ÷ capacity) × 100 for the SGCluster pod volumes. A full disk stops the database. Thresholds at 85% / 95%.

display.name: WAL size
display.description: pg_wal_size_bytes per pod. Unbounded growth means an orphan slot or a broken archiver, and a full disk next.

display.name: XID age · % of autovacuum_freeze_max_age
display.description: pg_database_datfrozenxid_age ÷ autovacuum_freeze_max_age (default 200 million). At 100% anti-wraparound autovacuum is forced; real wraparound is near 1,000% (2^31). Amber at 100%, red at 150%.

display.description: pg_stat_archiver_last_archive_age, minimum across pods (a replica freezes the value at the last failover). Above 300 s, WAL is not reaching the backup.
